name: @waste/db
description: The database foundation (Issue #64): the Drizzle schema of the `wms` Postgres schema, its SQL migrations, the pieces every domain table is built from, and the demo seed (`pnpm db:seed`). It holds Organisation & Access (Issue #70), the fifteen Registry tables — the catalogue, customers and their properties, agreements and subscriptions, containers and their effective-dated service placements (Issue #78) — the nine Planning tables: planning areas with their effective-dated boundaries, collection calendars with their holidays, route schemes with their collection groups and each group's stop matching rule or picked containers (Issue #97), and the thirteen Resources tables: vehicle types and their compatibility with container types, depots, warehouses, unloading stations and their fractions, vehicles with their compartments, drivers, the append-only stock movement ledger with its asset-state query, and vehicle allocations with their append-only events (Issue #101), and the seven Execution tables: the dated route with its planned and actual assignment, its pickups carrying the place and fraction on the service date, the driver's session, the append-only proof of service and unload ledgers, the append-only receipt of every driver command keyed by the client's id, and the outbox, beside the company's route-number counter, the sync role wms_sync and the powersync publication over the synced tables (Issue #104), and the three Resolution tables: the ticket with its links into the four contexts before it, its append-only history of status changes, assignments and comments, and the alert, beside the company's ticket-number counter and the outbox's grown vocabulary (Issue #109), and the sixteen Finance & Contracting tables: the price list and its rows keyed on a generated condition set, the service area with its two sets and its assignments, the provider's effective-dated prices, the billable event whose status is a reading, the billing run with its exclusions ledger, the invoice and invoice-line ledgers, the settlement with its lines and its history ledger, and the weight-review ledger with its projection, beside the company's invoice-number counter, the product's invoicing columns, the agreement's price list and the unload's project key (Issue #112). Since Issue #109 part B it also holds the write statements both processes run (`src/commands/`: the ticket-opening statements, the alert link, the outbox's one writer, the Resolution rows on the wire, generation's queue and job payload, the row lock, the document counter and the refusal a statement throws in place of the API's problem), the process id minter (`src/ids.ts`) and the SQLSTATE readers (`src/sqlstate.ts`), each re-exported by the API under the name its routes always used. Server-only: consumed by apps/api and the worker, never by apps/web (ADR-0001; the root ESLint config refuses the import there). Ships TypeScript source like every workspace package.
